surface_forms: un jeune homme du grand monde

appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Norpois me présentait aussi, dans les termes les plus chaleureux ; puis trois hypothèses : « Peut-être trouvait-il commode de me faire une politesse qui n'entamait en rien son crédit puisque je venais justement d'être présenté ; peut-être parce qu'il pensait qu'un étranger, même illustre, était moins au courant des salons français... ; peut-être pour exercer une de ses prérogatives... ou par le goût d'archaïsme ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator immediately dissolves Norpois's warm second presentation into a series of costless, self-serving motives (credit preserved, a foreigner's ignorance, prerogative, antiquarian vanity), so the apparent generosity is retrospectively deflated. All three conjectures point the same way, so the deflation is the narrator's own and is carried by the passage, not merely floated.

appraisal_events.evidence: « N'est-ce pas, monsieur l'ambassadeur, que Mme Leroi est une personne sans intérêt, très inférieure à toutes celles qui fréquentent ici, et que j'ai eu raison de ne pas l'attirer ? » — « M. de Norpois se contenta de répondre par un salut plein de respect mais vide de signification. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Villeparisis solicits public ratification of her disparagement of Mme Leroi, and Norpois withholds it with a bow that is formally deferential but explicitly empty; the narrator has already exposed her motive as a need to be told she has nothing to regret, and she must cover the failure by laughing off into an anecdote.

status_effects.explanation: His conspicuously warm gesture is locally recast as a piece of costless self-interested ceremony, lowering how the passage invites us to appraise him even as his ambassadorial weight is acknowledged.
Her leading question fails: she gets a meaningless bow instead of the endorsement she engineered, and has to change the subject herself.
The narrator frames her attack as a need for reassurance about a woman she does not know, which exposes the regret she is denying.
The disparagement aimed at her is pointedly not ratified by the authority whose confirmation was sought, so the absent Mme Leroi comes off locally better than the attack intends.
He is presented to a prince by two sponsors, including an ambassador in the warmest terms, an archaic double honor — though the narrator's own gloss keeps the gain formal rather than substantive.

ambiguities: The narrator offers two alternative causes for Norpois's empty bow — « Soit indépendance, soit fatigue » — so it is undetermined whether the non-ratification is a deliberate refusal to back Mme de Villeparisis or mere indifference; the local effect on her rhetorical position is the same either way, which is why E2 is still read as a snub.

« le prince » / « cette Altesse » is an unnamed foreign highness who cannot be resolved to any reference-sheet entity and is not a reviewed unnamed figure, so he is excluded from characters_present despite being the addressee of the presentation.
